knowledge:
- key_parameters: <mincov=minimum read coverage per base required to retain a methylation call (default is 10) ;; treatment=integer vector defining sample group membership (e.g., 1 for test, 0 for control) ;; context=methylation context to read, typically "CpG", "CHG", or "CHH" ;; dbtype=set to "tabix" to store methylation data in an external bgzipped flat-file database instead of in-memory ;; destrand=logical in unite() indicating whether to merge reads from both strands of a CpG dinucleotide (only for CpG context) ;; overdispersion=set to "MN" in calculateDiffMeth() to apply overdispersion correction, which automatically switches the statistical test to an F-test ;; covariates=a data.frame of covariates (e.g., age, sex) to include in the logistic regression model to control for confounding factors>
- alternatives: <MEDIPS=preferred for affinity-based methods like MIRA-Seq or MeDIP-Seq ;; Bioconductor MethylationArray packages (e.g., minfi, ChAMP)=preferred for Illumina Methylation arrays (27K, 450k, EPIC) ;; methylDackel or Bismark methylation extractor=preferred for extracting methylation calls from local or spliced alignments (HISAT2 mode) before importing into methylKit>
- when_to_use: <When performing base-pair or regional resolution differential DNA methylation analysis and annotation on high-throughput bisulfite sequencing data (RRBS, WGBS, or variants) with or without replicates and covariates.>
- pitfalls: <Setting destrand=TRUE on non-CpG (CpH) methylation data will cause incorrect results ;; Using processBismarkAln() directly on local or spliced alignments is not supported; use external extractors first ;; Using select() or '[' on database-backed (methylDB) objects will return their in-memory equivalents, which may cause memory issues if the dataset is extremely large ;; regionCounts() sorts input regions by chromosome and position, so the output order may differ from the input GRanges order ;; Do not merge methylRaw objects of different contexts into a single methylRawList as they will not overlap correctly>

workflows.name: base_resolution_diff_meth
workflows.intent: Perform base-resolution differential methylation analysis, sample comparative analysis, and genomic annotation using in-memory objects.
input: file.list (list of text files containing methylation calls per sample)
gene.obj (transcript features object read from a BED file)
cpg.obj (CpG island and shore features read from a BED file)
workflows.stages: 1. Read methylation call files ;; 2. Filter samples by coverage ;; 3. Merge samples to find common covered bases ;; 4. Calculate sample correlation and perform clustering/PCA ;; 5. Calculate differential methylation ;; 6. Extract hyper/hypo-methylated bases ;; 7. Annotate differentially methylated bases with genic parts and CpG features
workflows.code:
myobj=methRead(file.list,
           sample.id=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),
           assembly="hg18",
           treatment=c(1,1,0,0),
           context="CpG",
           mincov = 10
           )
filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL,
                                      hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)
meth=unite(myobj, destrand=FALSE)
getCorrelation(meth,plot=TRUE)
clusterSamples(meth, dist="correlation", method="ward", plot=TRUE)
PCASamples(meth)
myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth)
myDiff25p=getMethylDiff(myDiff,difference=25,qvalue=0.01)
annotateWithGeneParts(as(myDiff25p,"GRanges"),gene.obj)
diffCpGann=annotateWithFeatureFlank(as(myDiff25p,"GRanges"),
                                    cpg.obj$CpGi,cpg.obj$shores,
                         feature.name="CpGi",flank.name="shores")

workflows.name: large_data_tabix_db
workflows.intent: Read and manage large-scale bisulfite sequencing datasets using flat-file databases (Tabix) to minimize memory usage.
input: file.list (list of text files containing methylation calls per sample)
mydbpath (path to an existing tabix file)
workflows.stages: 1. Read raw files directly into a Tabix-backed methylRawListDB object ;; 2. Convert an in-memory object to a flat-file database ;; 3. Load an existing flat-file database using its file path
workflows.code:
myobjDB=methRead(file.list,
           sample.id=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),
           assembly="hg18",
           treatment=c(1,1,0,0),
           context="CpG",
           dbtype = "tabix",
           dbdir = "methylDB"
           )
objDB=makeMethylDB(methylBase.obj,"exMethylDB")
readMethylDB(mydbpath)

workflows.name: regional_and_tiling_analysis
workflows.intent: Summarize and analyze methylation levels over tiling windows or predefined genomic regions (e.g., promoters).
input: file.list (list of text files containing methylation calls per sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Read methylation call files with a relaxed coverage threshold ;; 2. Summarize counts over tiling windows ;; 3. Summarize counts over predefined genomic regions (promoters)
workflows.code:
myobj_lowCov = methRead(file.list,
           sample.id=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),
           assembly="hg18",
           treatment=c(1,1,0,0),
           context="CpG",
           mincov = 3
           )
tiles = tileMethylCounts(myobj_lowCov,win.size=1000,step.size=1000,cov.bases = 10)
promoters=regionCounts(myobj,gene.obj$promoters)

workflows.name: methylation_profile_segmentation
workflows.intent: Segment methylation or differential methylation profiles into regions of similar methylation levels.
input: mbw (methylBase object or RDS file containing methylation data)
workflows.stages: 1. Segment the methylation profiles ;; 2. Export the segmented regions to a BED file
